title: Air handling unit (AHU)
aliases: AHU; FAHU; fresh air handling unit; air handler
summary: A factory-built cabinet that filters, cools, dehumidifies and moves air for a building or zone. In the Gulf it is nearly always chilled-water, double-skin, and specified against Eurovent and EN 1886.
body: What a UAE or KSA specification usually fixes: casing class to EN 1886 (D1/L1/T2/TB2 or better), Eurovent-certified performance, ePM1 filtration, coated coils, plug fans with VFD, and a design ambient of 46 °C (UAE) to 48–50 °C (KSA). A fresh-air unit (FAHU) adds heat recovery because Gulf outdoor air at 46 °C / high humidity is the dominant load.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Fan coil unit (FCU)
summary: A small terminal unit — fan, chilled-water coil, filter and drain pan — serving one room or zone. Concealed ducted units dominate Gulf hotels, apartments and offices.
body: Gulf specifications turn on: 2-pipe cooling-only (heating is rare), high external static for ducted units, EC motors for energy codes, Eurovent-certified capacity, insulated drain pans with auxiliary pan, and coils rated for district-cooling water temperatures where Empower or Tabreed supply the site.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Air-cooled chiller
aliases: air cooled chiller; ACCH; packaged chiller
summary: A packaged outdoor machine that makes chilled water using refrigerant compressors and air-cooled condenser coils — no cooling tower, no water treatment. The Gulf default below about 1,500 TR.
body: The Gulf changes everything about a chiller selection: capacity is quoted at 46 °C ambient (not the AHRI 35 °C), the unit must keep running at 50–52 °C, condenser coils must survive salt and sand, and the electrical supply differs between the UAE (50 Hz) and KSA (60 Hz). Part-load efficiency (IPLV / ESEER) decides energy-code compliance; full-load EER decides the tender comparison.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: AHU casing and panels
summary: Double-skin sandwich panels, usually 50 mm, on a thermal-break frame. The casing class decides leakage, deflection and heat gain — all tested to EN 1886.
body: Gulf norm: 50 mm panels, PU foam or 40–60 kg/m³ mineral wool, outer skin pre-painted galvanised (PPGI) or aluzinc, inner skin galvanised; thermal bridging class TB2 or better so the outside never sweats at 46 °C / 80 % RH. Hospitals ask for stainless inner skin and hygienic (VDI 6022) construction.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Thermal-break frame
summary: The extruded aluminium or composite frame that stops heat conducting from the hot skin to the cold one. Without it, condensation forms on the outside of a Gulf AHU.
body: EN 1886 thermal bridging class TB1–TB5; specifications ask for TB2 or TB1. Check the pentapost frame, not just the panel.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Supply fan
summary: Moves the air. Modern Gulf AHUs use direct-driven plug (backward-curved) fans with a VFD or EC motor; belt-driven forward-curved fans are legacy.
body: Performance to AMCA 210 / ISO 5801; motors IE3 minimum, IE4 common; fan arrays (multiple small plug fans) for redundancy in data halls and hospitals. Specific fan power (SFP) is what Dubai Green Building and ASHRAE 90.1 limit.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Return / exhaust fan
summary: The second fan in a full AHU or heat-recovery FAHU, handling return or exhaust air. Same construction as the supply fan.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Chilled-water cooling coil
summary: Copper tubes, aluminium fins, 6–8 rows in Gulf fresh-air units to take 46 °C / 80 % RH air down to 12–14 °C. Rated to AHRI 410.
body: Face velocity 2.0–2.5 m/s keeps carry-over off the fins; fin spacing 8–12 fpi; 0.4–0.5 mm tube wall; hydrophilic or epoxy/e-coated fins where coastal. Entering/leaving water 6.7/12.2 °C on chillers, or 5.5/14.5 °C on district cooling — the coil is selected for the water the site actually has.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: DX cooling coil
summary: A direct-expansion coil for AHUs paired with VRV or condensing units instead of chilled water. Daikin sells this as a matched system.
body: Multiple circuits (up to four) for capacity staging; refrigerant R-410A or R-32 — the R-32 AHU coils Daikin now offers across Compact, Modular and Professional ranges.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Heat-recovery section
aliases: ERV; energy recovery; rotary wheel; plate heat exchanger
summary: A rotary wheel or plate exchanger that pre-cools incoming fresh air with the building's exhaust. The biggest single energy saver on a Gulf FAHU.
body: Enthalpy (sorption) wheels recover latent heat too, which is where the Gulf load is; plate exchangers avoid cross-contamination for hospitals. Efficiency to EN 308; Daikin Modular P uses a counter-flow plate, Modular R a rotary wheel.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Air filters
summary: Pre-filter plus fine filter as standard; HEPA for hospitals and clean areas. Classes now follow ISO 16890 (ePM10, ePM2.5, ePM1), which replaced EN 779 G/M/F classes.
body: Typical Gulf stack: ePM10 50 % (old G4) panel + ePM1 55–80 % (old F7–F9) bag or compact. Hospital: add H13/H14 HEPA to EN 1822. Sand and dust make filter pressure switches and generous filter face area non-negotiable.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Dampers
summary: Opposed-blade aluminium dampers on fresh, return and exhaust; motorised for economiser or mixing control.
body: Leakage class to EN 1751 (class 3 or 4 specified); fire and smoke dampers in the ductwork answer to the Civil Defence, not to the AHU.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Drain pan
summary: Collects condensate under the cooling coil. In the Gulf the coil is always wet, so the pan is sloped, insulated and stainless.
body: Stainless steel 304, double-sloped to the drain, trapped drain sized for negative fan pressure. Corroded or flat pans are the most common cause of AHU water damage.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: UV-C section
summary: Germicidal lamps mounted downstream of the coil to keep the wet coil and drain pan biologically clean. Common in hospital and hospitality specifications.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Sound attenuator
summary: Splitter silencers on supply or return to meet room NC levels. Often factory-fitted as an AHU section.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: AHU control panel
summary: The DDC controller, VFD and sensors — temperature, humidity, CO₂, filter DP — wired at the factory, talking BACnet or Modbus to the BMS.
body: Daikin ships its AHUs with or without Daikin Digital Control (up to 310 I/O); a factory-tested panel removes the site commissioning risk that a loose-supplied panel brings.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Airflow
summary: The volume of air the unit moves, in m³/h or CFM. The first number on any schedule.
body: Daikin Professional reaches 144,000 m³/h; Modular P 20,000 m³/h; Compact L/T 3,450–4,200 m³/h.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: External static pressure (ESP)
summary: The pressure the fan must overcome outside the unit — ductwork, diffusers, filters downstream. Wrong ESP is the most common reason an installed AHU under-delivers.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Casing leakage class
summary: EN 1886 class L1 (tightest) to L3 for air leakage through the casing at −400 Pa and +700 Pa. Gulf specifications call L1 or L2.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Casing deflection class
summary: EN 1886 class D1 to D3 for how far panels bow under pressure. D1 for hospitals and pressurised units.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Thermal transmittance class
summary: EN 1886 class T1 to T5 for heat gain through the casing. T2 is the Gulf norm; T1 for very cold supply air.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Thermal bridging class
summary: EN 1886 class TB1 to TB5. Decides whether the outside of the casing sweats in Gulf humidity. Ask for TB2 or better.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Filter bypass leakage class
summary: EN 1886 class F9 to F5 for air that sneaks around the filter frame. Matters more than filter class in a dusty climate.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Specific fan power (SFP)
summary: Fan power divided by airflow, W per l/s or kW per m³/s. Energy codes (ASHRAE 90.1, Dubai Green Building) cap it.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Sound power level
summary: Noise radiated to the duct and to the plant room, in dB(A) per octave band. Selected with the attenuator, not after it.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU fan and motor
summary: Forward-curved centrifugal blowers; EC (brushless DC) motors now, three-speed PSC motors before. EC is what makes an FCU pass an energy audit.
body: EC motor: 0–10 V or Modbus speed control, 50–70 % less power than PSC at part speed. Daikin concealed units run four usable speeds with self-diagnosis.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU coil
summary: Copper-tube, aluminium-fin coil of 3 or 4 rows; 4 rows where district cooling supplies 5.5 °C water at a high ΔT, or where humidity control matters.
body: Rated to AHRI 440 / Eurovent at 45/55 °F (7/12 °C) entering/leaving water; a district-cooling site needs re-rating at its own temperatures, which most selection software can do.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU drain pan
summary: Insulated pan under the coil, with an auxiliary pan under the valve set. The single most common FCU call-back in the Gulf is a leaking or sweating pan.
body: Polypropylene or stainless, closed-cell insulation, sloped to the drain; condensate pump where gravity drain is impossible.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU filter
summary: Washable nylon or aluminium mesh, G2–G3 class. Site dust means it is cleaned quarterly, so access is a design point.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU casing
summary: Galvanised steel, 10–20 mm internal insulation, with hanging brackets. Concealed ducted units are the Gulf norm; cassette and exposed units for retail and lobbies.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU control valve
summary: Two-way on/off or modulating valve on the return, or a pressure-independent control valve (PICV) where the chilled-water system is variable-flow.
body: Valveless units are offered where the valve is supplied separately; Daikin quotes both. PICVs are increasingly required by district-cooling providers to protect their ΔT.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU thermostat / controller
summary: Room thermostat with fan speed and setpoint, wired or wireless; BMS-connected units carry a Modbus or BACnet controller.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Cooling capacity (total and sensible)
summary: Total capacity removes heat and moisture; sensible capacity is the part that lowers temperature. Gulf loads are latent-heavy, so both are checked.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU external static pressure
summary: What a ducted unit can push against. Standard 30–50 Pa; high-static 100–200 Pa for long duct runs in villas and hotel corridors.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Chilled-water entering / leaving temperature
summary: The water the coil is rated at. Chiller sites: 6.7/12.2 °C (44/54 °F). District cooling: 5.5/14.5 °C or 5.5/16 °C, a much higher ΔT.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU sound level
summary: NC or dB(A) at each fan speed, measured to ISO 3741. Bedrooms are usually held to NC 30–35 at medium speed.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: FCU power input
summary: Watts drawn at each speed. EC units are compared on this line; PSC units lose.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Compressor
aliases: screw compressor; scroll compressor; inverter compressor
summary: The heart of the chiller. Air-cooled Gulf units use scroll (tandem/trio) up to about 200 TR, screw — fixed-speed or inverter — from 150 to 600+ TR, and oil-free magnetic-bearing centrifugal in premium ranges.
body: Inverter screw (Daikin EWAD-TZ, York YVAA) wins on part-load efficiency, which is how energy codes are met; fixed-speed screw wins on price. Scroll ranges (Daikin EWAT-B on R-32, York YLAA) cover the small end.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Air-cooled condenser coil
summary: Rejects heat to the outside air. Microchannel aluminium (MCHE) or round-tube plate-fin copper/aluminium. Coastal and industrial sites need a protective coating.
body: MCHE: less refrigerant, lighter, but harder to repair and needs a proven coating (e-coat) near the sea. RTPF with epoxy or Blygold coating is the conservative Gulf choice. Sand loading argues for wider fin spacing and hinged coil guards for cleaning.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Condenser fans
summary: Axial fans, now EC or VFD-driven, that pull air across the condenser. Speed control is how the chiller holds head pressure at 20 °C and 50 °C alike.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Evaporator
summary: Where refrigerant chills the water: shell-and-tube (flooded, falling-film or DX) on screw units, brazed-plate on scroll units.
body: Gulf specifications often ask for a fouling factor of 0.044 m²K/kW instead of the AHRI 0.0176, and for glycol only in process jobs; check the freeze protection logic when the plant sits idle in winter.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Refrigerant
summary: The working fluid. R-134a and its lower-GWP drop-in R-513A on screw units; R-410A giving way to R-32 or R-454B on scroll units; R-1234ze on some oil-free ranges.
body: GWP is not yet regulated in the UAE or KSA the way the EU F-gas rule does, but Kigali ratification and green-building credits make low-GWP a tender advantage. Safety classification to ASHRAE 34: R-32 and R-454B are A2L (mildly flammable), which affects plant-room and roof siting.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Electronic expansion valve
summary: Meters refrigerant into the evaporator; electronic control is what allows stable operation across the Gulf ambient swing.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Chiller control panel
summary: The unit controller (Daikin MicroTech, York Smart Connect / OptiView) with BACnet or Modbus to the BMS, plus VFDs, soft starters and phase protection.
body: Ask for: remote setpoint, demand limit, run hours per compressor, refrigerant leak alarm, and a cloud link (Daikin on Site, JCI Connected) where the operator wants it.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Integrated pump package
summary: Factory-mounted chilled-water pumps, expansion tank and strainer on the chiller frame. Saves a plant room on small sites; check redundancy.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Sound attenuation package
summary: Low-noise fans, compressor acoustic jackets, and night-mode fan limits. Needed wherever a chiller sits near residences.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: High-ambient package
summary: Larger condenser surface, uprated fans and motors, and control limits that keep the chiller online at 50–55 °C instead of tripping. Standard in KSA, common in UAE.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Cooling capacity at design ambient
summary: The capacity the chiller delivers at the site ambient — 46 °C in most UAE specs, 46–50 °C in KSA — not the 35 °C AHRI rating. A chiller loses roughly 20–25 % between the two.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Full-load EER / COP
summary: Cooling output over electrical input at full load and design conditions. The number tenders compare; energy codes set minimums.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Part-load efficiency (IPLV / ESEER)
summary: A weighted average of efficiency at 100/75/50/25 % load. IPLV per AHRI 550/590, ESEER per Eurovent. This is where inverter and oil-free machines earn their price.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Ambient operating range
summary: The outdoor temperature band the chiller runs in — up to 52 °C or 55 °C with a high-ambient package, and down to the winter minimum with head-pressure control.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Chilled-water temperatures and ΔT
summary: Leaving and entering water: 6.7/12.2 °C (44/54 °F) is the AHRI default; Gulf specifications use it or 5.5/12.2 °C; larger ΔT lowers pump energy.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Power supply
summary: UAE: 400 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz. KSA: 380 V, 3-phase, 60 Hz. The same model number is a different unit — motors, fans, VFDs and capacity all change with frequency.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Chiller sound power
summary: Sound power in dB(A) to ISO 9614 or ISO 3744, at full and part load. Night-time limits near residential plots are set by the municipality.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Minimum turndown
summary: The lowest stable load the chiller can hold before cycling — 10–15 % on inverter screw and oil-free units, higher on scroll. Matters for hotels at 3 a.m.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: EN 1886
summary: The European test for AHU casings: mechanical strength (D), air leakage (L), filter bypass (F), thermal transmittance (T) and thermal bridging (TB) — each a class.
body: The classes a Gulf specification quotes: D1 / L1 (or L2) / F9 / T2 / TB2. Eurovent-certified units publish these from third-party tests; unlisted units are claims.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: EN 13053
summary: Rating and performance of AHUs and their components as a whole — how the numbers on the datasheet are to be measured.
body: The companion to EN 1886; together they are what "Eurovent AHU certified" means.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: Eurovent Certified Performance — AHU
summary: Third-party certification of AHU casing classes and thermal/acoustic performance, with a public directory of certified ranges and software.
body: Widely specified in UAE and KSA because it lets a consultant check a claim without a test. Daikin Professional and Systemair Geniox are certified ranges; confirm each model size on the Eurovent directory.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: AHRI 410
summary: US rating standard for forced-circulation air-cooling and heating coils. The coil capacity on an AHU or FCU datasheet is stated to it.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: AMCA 210 / ISO 5801
summary: Laboratory methods for testing fans for aerodynamic performance. A fan curve is only a fan curve if it was taken to one of these.
body: AMCA-licensed fans carry the certified ratings seal; AMCA 300 covers sound.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: ISO 16890
summary: The current filter classification by particle size (ePM1, ePM2.5, ePM10, coarse), which replaced EN 779 G/M/F classes in 2018.
body: Specifications still written as G4 + F7 translate to roughly ePM10 50 % + ePM1 55 %. Ask the filter maker for the ISO 16890 rating, not a conversion.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: EN 1822
summary: Classification and testing of HEPA and ULPA filters (H13, H14, U15…). Required for operating theatres, isolation rooms, pharma and clean rooms.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: EN 1751
summary: Air-terminal and damper leakage classes. A specification asking for "class 3" or "class 4" dampers means this standard.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: EN 308
summary: Test method for the effectiveness of air-to-air heat recovery devices — wheels, plates, run-around coils.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: ASHRAE 62.1
summary: Ventilation for acceptable indoor air quality: the fresh-air rates most Gulf codes adopt, which size the FAHU.
body: Dubai and Abu Dhabi building regulations reference it; hospitals use ASHRAE 170 instead.
source_ref: Manufacturer catalogues and Gulf specifications — verify against the current edition

title: ASHRAE 90.1
summary: The US energy standard for buildings, adopted or referenced by Gulf green-building regulations for fan power, chiller efficiency and economiser rules.
body: Chiller minimum efficiencies in Table 6.8.1 (path A / path B) are what Dubai and Estidama compliance tables are derived from.

title: ASHRAE 170
summary: Ventilation of health-care facilities: air changes, filtration and pressure relationships for hospitals. Drives HEPA and 100 % fresh-air AHUs in Gulf hospitals.

title: NFPA 90A
summary: US fire-safety standard for air-conditioning and ventilating systems: smoke detectors, fire dampers, duct materials. Adopted by Gulf civil-defence codes.

title: UL 1995 / EN 60335-2-40
summary: Product safety standards for heating and cooling equipment (UL, US) and for electrical heat pumps, air conditioners and dehumidifiers (IEC/EN). A unit sold in the Gulf is listed to one or both.

title: VDI 6022 / DIN 1946-4
summary: German hygiene standards for AHUs (VDI 6022) and hospital ventilation (DIN 1946-4). "Hygienic AHU" in a Gulf hospital tender means built and certified to these.

title: AHRI 440
summary: US rating standard for room fan-coil units: capacity, airflow and power at 45/55 °F water. FCU datasheets quote it.

title: Eurovent Certified Performance — Fan coil units
summary: Third-party certification of fan-coil capacity, airflow, power and sound, tested to EN 1397. The Gulf consultant's check on an FCU claim.

title: ISO 3741
summary: Determination of sound power in a reverberation room. FCU and small-unit sound data is taken to it.

title: AHRI 550/590
summary: US rating standard for water-chilling packages: full-load EER/kW per ton and IPLV at AHRI conditions (35 °C ambient, 44/54 °F water). The universal tender baseline; the Gulf then re-rates at 46 °C.

title: Eurovent Certified Performance — Chillers (LCP-HP)

title: SASO 2874
summary: Saudi standard for the minimum energy performance of large-capacity air conditioners, including chillers, above the SASO 2663 ceiling of 70,000 Btu/h. Registration on the Saudi Label & Standard (SLS) portal is required to ship.

title: SASO 2663

title: UAE.S 5010 (ESMA / MoIAT)
summary: The UAE energy-efficiency standards and labels for air conditioners, enforced through the ECAS certificate of conformity by ESMA (now within MoIAT). Higher minimum EERs took effect 1 January 2021.

title: UAE market — what changes for AHU, FCU and chillers
aliases: UAE; Dubai; Abu Dhabi; United Arab Emirates
summary: Power 400 V / 3 ph / 50 Hz; design ambient 46 °C; Dubai Green Building Regulations and Estidama set efficiency; Eurovent certification is the consultant's check; coastal corrosion and district cooling shape the selections.
body: Authorities: Dubai Municipality (DM) and DEWA in Dubai; DMT and Estidama in Abu Dhabi; Trakhees in the free zones; Civil Defence for fire and smoke.
